2 Independent analysis of the abstracts

2.1 A Multistage Extraction Pipeline for Long Scanned Financial Documents

Topic/motivation Clearly reported Applying end-to-end recent vision-language models to full financial reports often leads to unreliable extraction due to their noisy and non-machine readable nature. No evidence in the abstract.

Research question Clearly reported, implicit Whether multi-stage extraction framework leads to more accuracy.

Empirical basis Present but ambiguous The dataset comprises 120 production KYC documents, 3000 scanned pages. What is missing is the language, how the ground truth was produced.

Method Clearly stated They report the components pipeline and they use ablations to derive the importance of each component.

Observed outcomes Clearly stated They observe that the proposed pipeline consistently outperforms baselines and pick a best configuration at 87.27% accuracy. Furthermore, thanks to ablation studies, page-retrival in the most dominant contributor.

Findings Clearly stated A key design choice is separating page localization from multimodal reasoning.

Strengths The problem->experiment structure is cleanly explained.

Limitations Underspecified baseline; unclear how performance varies among different kind pf configurations; no information on annotation or field types; no information if the dataset has already natural ground truth labels.

2.2 VAREX: A Benchmark for Multi-Modal Structured Extraction from Documents

Topic/motivation Clearly reported Existing benchmarks evaluate extraction from a single input representation, so the impact of the input format on accuracy is not isolated.

Research question Clearly reported, implicit How does the input modality affect extraction accuracy, and where do small models ( ≤ 4B) fail?

Empirical basis Clearly reported 1,798 documents, a unique schema per document, three structural categories, four modalities each, 20 models evaluated. Values are synthetic (templates filled programmatically). What is missing is the language of the forms, what this categories are, and the names of the models.

Method Clearly reported The study combines benchmark construction and systematic ablation of how input format affects extraction accuracy.

Observed outcomes Ambiguous Schema echo depresses scores by 45-65 pp in affected models; 2B fine-tuning gives +81 pp; layout-preserving text gives +3-18 pp, more than images; benchmark discriminates best in the 60-95% band. Absolute scores absent; "+81 pp" has no stated starting point.

Findings Clearly reported Below 4B the bottleneck is output compliance, not extraction capability; the deficit can be fixed with fine-tuning; layout cues in text beat pixel cues. Each finding is written in the same clause as the observation it comes from.

Strengths Precise gap statement; benchmark size and design are given numerically; every finding comes with a magnitude.
